question: Explain the saturation property of nuclear force. Why does this property support the nearly constant density of nuclei?

options.A: Saturation means each nucleon interacts strongly mainly with its nearest neighbours, not with all nucleons. Because nuclear force is short-ranged, nuclear volume grows approximately in proportion to nucleon number; mass and volume both scale with $A$, so nuclear density remains nearly constant.
options.B: Saturation means each nucleon attracts every other nucleon equally, making density increase sharply with mass number.
options.C: Saturation means nuclear force becomes stronger over atomic distances, so nuclear density decreases with $A$.
options.D: Saturation means nucleons do not interact at all, so nuclear density is zero.
